name: Fender Bassman 5F6-A (1959 tweed, 4x10)
description: Fender 5F6-A Bassman as drawn on the Fender factory schematic. Two input channels (Normal and Bright, Input 1 of each: two 68 kΩ stoppers in parallel, 1 MΩ to ground) into a 12AY7 whose two triodes share one 820 Ω / 250 µF cathode (100 kΩ plates), 0.02 µF into a 1 MΩ audio volume per channel (Bright has 100 pF from the top of the pot to the wiper), mixed through two 270 kΩ resistors onto the 12AX7 second stage (100 kΩ plate, 820 Ω unbypassed cathode), DC-coupled into the 12AX7 cathode follower (100 kΩ cathode resistor) that drives the treble/bass/middle stack (250 pF, 56 kΩ slope, 0.02 µF bass and middle caps, 250 kΩ treble, 1 MΩ bass, 25 kΩ middle). 0.02 µF into the 12AX7 long-tail-pair phase inverter (82 kΩ / 100 kΩ plates, 470 Ω shared cathode, 1 MΩ grid leaks, 10 kΩ tail, 47 pF across the plates); 27 kΩ global feedback from the 2 Ω speaker tap enters the bottom of the tail and, through the 0.1 µF bypass, the second grid; the 5 kΩ presence pot sits between that node and ground with 0.1 µF on its wiper. 0.1 µF / 220 kΩ into two 5881 (6L6GC model) at fixed bias (-48 V from the 15 kΩ / 56 kΩ / 8 µF bias network), screens through 470 Ω, 4 kΩ : 2 Ω output transformer (Fender/Triad 45249) into four 8 Ω 10-inch speakers in parallel. Supply: 325-0-325 V winding, 5AR4/GZ34, 2 x 20 µF at the OT centre tap (A), 4 H choke to the screens (B, 20 µF), 4.7 kΩ to the phase inverter (C, 20 µF), 10 kΩ to the preamp (B+4, 8 µF). Standby switch and anti-pop cap omitted (standby closed).

sources.title: Fender Musical Instruments, 'Fender Bassman Schematic, Model 5F6-A' (factory schematic with voltage chart; annotated reproduction by Rob Robinette)
Rob Robinette, '5F6A Mods' (How the Bassman Works, How the Long Tail Pair Phase Inverter Works, Fender Mid-Production 5F6A Circuit Changes, bias network, power transformer)
Rob Robinette, 5F6-A Bassman layout (pot values and tapers: volume 1M log, treble 250K lin, bass 1M log, middle 25K lin)
R. Kuehnel, 'The Fender Bassman 5F6-A Circuit' (Pentode Press summary): 12AY7 first stage, OT 45249 4k primary / 2 Ω secondary, PT 8087 325-0-325 V, choke 14684, 27k feedback from the 2 Ω tap

D. T. Yeh and J. O. Smith, 'Discretization of the 59 Fender Bassman tone stack', DAFx 2006: C1 0.25 nF, C2 = C3 20 nF, R1 250k, R2 1M, R3 25k, R4 56k; treble and middle linear, bass log; middle pot as a divider with C3 on the wiper
Ampbooks, 'Fender Bassman 5F6-A Circuit Analysis' (operating points: 12AY7 shared 820 Ω / 250 µF, V2A 820 Ω unbypassed, LTP, 5881 load line 1 kΩ per tube = 4 kΩ plate-to-plate)
R. McLean, 12AY7 / 6072 Koren-form SPICE model fitted to an Electro-Harmonix 6072A/12AY7EH (16 June 2005), diyAudio thread 'PSpice/LTSpice model for 12AY7/6072 wanted'
Hammond 1750K datasheet (drop-in replacement for Fender 45249/125A9A): 4000 Ω CT primary, 2 Ω secondary, primary DCR 89.43 Ω, secondary 0.180 Ω
Hammond 290DX datasheet (replacement for Fender 8087): 325-0-325 V at 230 mA, 356.1 V no-load per half, HT DCR 70.27 Ω red-red, primary 1.262 Ω, 50 V bias tap
Music Electronics Forum / Evatco 5F6-A parts list: choke 14684 is about 3.5-4 H, 90 mA, about 35-45 Ω DCR
Reverb listings of original Triad 45249 output transformers: measured DCR 41.2 Ω and 47.5 Ω per half primary, 0.2 Ω secondary
N. Koren, 'Improved vacuum tube models for SPICE simulations': 12AX7 and 6L6GC plate laws (library models)

io.note: outputVoltsPerFS calibrated (2026-11-09) to the mean RMS match gain (-14.2 dB) of the circuit_ab settings against the legacy model, so the A/B sits at the legacy loudness on average across clean and driven settings; final level is a listening-review decision

controls.label: Normal Volume
controls.note: Normal channel 1 MΩ audio-taper volume (no bright cap)

controls.label: Bright Volume
controls.note: Bright channel 1 MΩ audio-taper volume with 100 pF from the top of the pot to the wiper

controls.label: Bass
controls.note: 1 MΩ audio taper as a rheostat

controls.label: Middle
controls.note: 25 kΩ linear, wired as a divider: top to the bass pot, bottom to ground, wiper to the 0.02 µF middle cap

controls.label: Presence
controls.note: 5 kΩ pot between the feedback node (bottom of the PI tail) and ground, 0.1 µF from the wiper to ground: clockwise shunts the high frequencies of the feedback

controls.label: Power
controls.note: Legacy 'Power' parameter. The 5F6-A has only a mains switch and a standby switch; the circuit always runs powered with standby closed. Stored for preset round-trip, no circuit meaning.

controls.label: VAC
controls.note: Variac: scales the mains (every transformer secondary, including the bias winding) from 75 % at 0 through nominal at 0.5 to 108 % at 1 (90 / 120 / 130 VAC on a 120 V amp)
controls.modNote: Not on the original amplifier: a variac on the mains, as players did to run the amp at lower line voltage. Offered as a mod; at full scale the amp sees its rated mains.

controls.label: Sag
controls.note: Legacy supply-sag amount. Sag here emerges from the 5AR4, winding resistance, choke and filter caps; there is no knob. Stored, no circuit meaning.

controls.label: Response
controls.note: Legacy 'Response' (dynamics/feel) control. No such part in the 5F6-A. Stored, no circuit meaning.

controls.label: Bias
controls.note: Legacy power-tube bias knob. The 5F6-A bias is fixed (15k/56k divider, about -48 V); there is no bias pot. Stored, no circuit meaning.

controls.label: Vintage Mode
controls.note: Legacy 'Vintage Mode' switch. The circuit is already the vintage 5F6-A; there is nothing to switch. Stored, no circuit meaning.

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Catalogue stereo parameter; the circuit is mono, stored only

parts.label: HT winding, half A (325 Vrms)
parts.note: PT 8087, 325-0-325 Vrms per the schematic and Kuehnel; 460 V peak. Assumes the schematic's 117 V mains

parts.label: HT half-winding resistance
parts.note: Derived, not measured on an original 8087: Hammond 290DX (the 8087 replacement) DCR 70.27 Ω red-red = 35.1 Ω per half, plus the 1.262 Ω primary reflected by (356/120)^2 = 11.1 Ω. PT leakage inductance not modelled

parts.label: HT half-winding resistance
parts.note: see RWA

parts.label: Filter A (20 µF 600 V), in parallel
Choke DCR
parts.note: unverified: choke 14684 DCR quoted 35-45 Ω by forum/parts-list sources; 40 Ω used

parts.label: Choke 14684
parts.note: unverified: choke 14684 quoted as 3.5-4 H at 90 mA (Evatco parts list, Music Electronics Forum); 4 H used, no saturation

parts.label: Filter C, phase inverter (20 µF 600 V)
Bias rectifier output
parts.note: unverified: the real bias supply is a selenium/diode half-wave rectifier from a low-voltage PT tap (about 50 Vac) into 8 µF; modelled as an ideal DC source at the first bias filter node, value chosen so the 15k/56k divider gives the schematic's -48 V (-48 x 71/56). Ripple of the bias supply not modelled

parts.label: Bright Input 1 jack 1 MΩ
parts.note: Both channels' Input 1 jacks are driven from the one input (as with a Y cable or jumpered channels); VN/VB set each channel's level. The two 1 MΩ jack resistors load the source in parallel (500 kΩ) when io.sourceImpedance is used

parts.label: Bright grid stopper (Input 2 path, switched to Input 1 when Input 2 is empty)
V2B cathode follower (DC-coupled from V2A plate)
Slope resistor 56k
parts.note: Schematic and Yeh & Smith value. Robinette reports most production amps had 100k here

parts.label: Bass cap 0.02 µF
parts.note: Schematic and Yeh & Smith value. Robinette reports most production amps had 0.1 µF here

parts.label: V3A grid leak (to the tail junction)
V3B grid leak (to the tail junction)
V3B grid bypass 0.1 µF 200 V (to the feedback node)
PI tail 10k
parts.note: Schematic value. Robinette reports most production amps had 6.8k 2 W

parts.label: Presence 5k
parts.note: unverified taper: schematic gives 5k only; production amps used a 25k linear pot with 4.7k across it (Robinette). Linear assumed

parts.label: Global feedback 27k from the 2 Ω tap
Stability cap 47 pF between the PI plates
V5 grid leak 220k
parts.note: No grid stoppers on the 5F6-A schematic; the grids connect straight to the coupling caps

parts.label: V4 5881
parts.note: 5881 modelled with the library 6L6GC Koren set (near-identical curves per Kuehnel; 5881 is rated 23 W versus 30 W)

parts.label: V5 5881
parts.note: see V4

parts.label: Output transformer 45249 (4 kΩ : 2 Ω)
parts.note: 4 kΩ plate-to-plate per Kuehnel, Robinette and the Hammond 1750K drop-in replacement (4000 Ω CT; consistent with Ampbooks' 1 kΩ per-tube load line); the task's 'about 2 kΩ' was not found in any source. Secondary turns 2/sqrt(4000/2). DCR from measured originals (41.2/47.5 Ω, 0.2 Ω); which half goes to which plate is unknown. unverified: leakage 5 mH per half (8 mH and above makes the global NFB loop burst into a 30-60 kHz oscillation at medium drive, confirmed in ngspice; 5-7 mH is stable), lm 5 H (20 H plate-to-plate), lsat 1.5 V·s are typical-class values, not measured

parts.label: OT half-primary capacitance (A)
parts.note: unverified: half-primary self-capacitance with its loss as a lumped 470 pF + 2.2 kOhm from the plate to the centre tap (engine lesson from the AB763 Twin: a lossless lumped capacitance rings with the leakage and the NFB turns it into an oscillation; no capacitance gives kilovolt flyback spikes)
